searchText: <@213672586264051717> Do you need a strong guarantee, or is fuzzy acceptable? Like 99% of the time you'll correctly identify an intersection, and 1% of the time you'll miss an intersection. Can the sets be sorted, and is there a requirement for fast set updates, or fast comparisons, or both? Do you care about memory usage, or can you have an index? <@!301186049323958275> Oh yes, I meant to mention that. Strong would be ideal but fuzzy is acceptable. * We could have sorted sets as the input, yes. * We don't need to update the data structure. Once the set is finalized we can compute this hypothetical structure and pass it around. Since it'd be going over the network at a 1-1 correspondence with transactions (althogh packaged in blocks) it would have to be very space efficient. So we're looking for a no-update, space-efficient, comparision-efficient, possible fuzzy, structure. You could do something like a bloom filter. Given a sufficiently large bloom filter, you can get pretty close to accurate (fuzzy) answer as to whether there is an intersection between the sets. I think? (my experience with bloom filters is very limited)
